FFactoryze SPEC GUIDE
PRODUCT SPEC / V0.6Original document ↗

Learning to code with AI takes more than a working answer.

Factoryze is an open-source desktop coding environment for Windows, macOS, and Linux. It teaches and measures two skills: asking an agent precise questions, and judging what the agent does next.

01 / THE EXPERIENCE

What a student actually does

In a timed lab, the student works in a familiar editor with an agent pane, a visible token budget, and a task to solve.

01
⌨

Describe the change

The student prompts the agent. The judge scores specificity; practice mode can block vague prompts.

02
✳

Work with the agent

The agent reads files, edits code, and uses tools. A per-student budget keeps usage visible.

03
◫

Review each action

Diffs and shell commands appear as approval cards. Some mistakes are deliberate trials.

04
✓

Submit and reflect

Hidden checks and the event log produce a report on correctness, efficiency, prompts, and verification.

↗

The central idea: “Replace the nested loop with a set lookup” shows understanding. “Make it faster” asks the agent to explore and guess. Factoryze measures that difference—and whether the student catches bad work.

03 / ARCHITECTURE

Two seams make the system flexible

The IDE talks to an agent through ACP. The agent talks to a model through the engine gateway. That keeps the interface and measurement consistent across profiles.

DESKTOP APPTheia workbench

Editor · terminal · agent pane
Approval cards and diffs

ACPAgent ↔ IDE
PLUGGABLE PROFILEAgent process

Factoryze harness · OpenCode
Codex · Claude Code

GatewayAgent ↔ model
ENGINETrust & measurement

Model key · token meter · trials
Workspace mirror · grader

🔒

The key stays server-side

In labs, agents use session tokens. The gateway holds the real provider key and enforces the budget.

⟳

Tools run near the code

In v0 labs, external agents use the student machine’s workspace and shell: PowerShell on Windows, Bash on macOS/Linux. Trusted tests and trial definitions stay on the server.

04 / AGENTS

Agent profiles are plug-ins

Each profile supplies an ACP connection, model gateway settings, permission configuration, and tool translation.

REFERENCE PROFILE

Factoryze harness

Our own lightweight agent. Its loop runs in the engine, giving exact trial targeting and control over dispatch.

V0 · bundled
EXTERNAL PROFILE

OpenCode

Native ACP and broad model support. The spec recommends it as the first external profile in v0.

V0 target · bundled
EXTERNAL PROFILE

Codex

Connects through an ACP adapter and the gateway’s OpenAI Responses endpoint.

V0.x · bundled target
EXTERNAL PROFILE

Claude Code

Connects through an ACP adapter. The user or IT installs it under Anthropic’s terms.

V0.x · user installed

Benchmarks run the same task and model across profiles. Budgets and efficiency baselines are always set per task × profile@version × model.

05 / ASSESSMENT

Four layers in the report

The final code matters most. The report also shows how economically and carefully the student reached it. Percentages below come from the spec’s example lab config.

Correctness50%

Hidden tests and checks on the final workspace mirror. Acts as a gate.

Efficiency20%

Weighted tokens and turns compared with that exact profile and model baseline.

Specificity15%

Judge scores, weighted toward prompts that produced accepted edits.

Verification15%

Trial outcomes, tests after edits, diff review, and approval decisions.

WHY THE BASELINE MATTERSCompare a student to the agent they actually used.

Different agents consume tokens differently. Efficiency is a ratio to the same profile@version + model baseline. That makes cross-profile results approximate, so graded labs pin one profile.

06 / TRIALS

Realistic mistakes, safe by design

One to three deterministic trials may appear in a lab. Students know the agent can make mistakes; the specific trial stays hidden until after the lab.

<≤

Code mutation

A plausible bug is inserted into an edit, such as an off-by-one boundary.

↪

Side effect

A planted file triggers an extra, unrelated edit after the agent reads it.

“ ”

Misleading context

A false hint in the workspace tempts the student toward a bad solution.

⌁

Supply chain

A package or command looks suspicious at the approval card, testing whether the student stops it.

◎

Safety rules that apply to every profile

  • Payloads are harmless even if run: decoy packages stay in the private index, URLs use .invalid, and planted “secrets” are fake.
  • Shell commands require approval for supply-chain trials; unsupported profiles skip those trials.
  • Only fired, supported trials count toward verification. A trial that never fires is reported as such.
07 / DELIVERY

Build the lab first

The first release focuses on students in labs, with solo practice alongside it. Hosted service and hiring features come later.

V0

Solo + self-hosted labs

Desktop app, ACP pane, Factoryze harness, one external profile, judge, trials, scoring, light integrity, benchmark CLI, 2–3 Python tasks, and instructor tools.

V1

Hosted

Factoryze operates the server. Language-server diagnostics for the agent are also planned.

V2

Hiring controls

Lockdown, remote execution, proctoring, SSO, and replay.

FIRST MILESTONE · 4–5 DAY SPIKE

Prove the difficult connections early

  1. Build branded Theia installers for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
  2. Drive OpenCode from the ACP pane; meter and rewrite one edit through a stub gateway.
  3. Run a thin Factoryze harness with basic tools, including PowerShell on Windows, and a simulated supply-chain trial.
  4. Benchmark one task through both profiles on the same model.
08 / DECISIONS TO MAKE

What is still open?

The spec is a draft. These choices affect rollout, packaging, and the first institution deployments.

Which open-source licence? 01

MIT or Apache-2.0 could favor adoption. AGPL-3.0 for the engine could protect the hosted offering.

How does Python reach offline labs? 02

Can uv download Python, or must installers bundle it for disconnected labs?

Where does the lab server run? 03

Choose a LAN machine or cloud VM. Remote execution would require more server capacity.

Are CSV grades enough? 04

Confirm whether institutions need an LMS-specific export.

Who signs the installers? 05

Assign ownership of Windows and macOS signing certificates.

Is separate Claude Code installation acceptable? 06

Its terms prevent bundling in the open-source distribution, so the user or IT would install it.

Marked as assumptions in v0.6

Lab size of 20–60 students; OpenCode’s plugin path for preventing dispatch of approved trial payloads; the Vercel AI SDK provider layer; the roughly 1.5× harness benchmark target; and the one-developer effort estimates.
